goal: Make access explanations show only sources that actual enforcement reads.
runtime_operation_scope: Migrate data/contracts/ai/tools.json through the reviewed runtime-contract path if task 05 adds read-only access explain or editor-handoff tools; never commit the runtime copy.
decisions: Effective-access explanation is a read model of enforcement inputs, not a dump of Django auth tables.
access.users.explain and access.open_editor are read-only, non-confirming tools authorized by a fresh manage_roles check or active superuser reserve; no access-domain mutation tool may be registered.

The explanation response contains no email, AD identity, raw Django permissions or complete object ACLs. Roles, superuser reserve, technical groups and memory groups remain separate; ACL/workflow are non-grant object-scoped constraints.
Inactive targets may show assigned memberships as facts but receive no effective capabilities or active superuser grants.

The access.open_editor tool accepts only target_type user|role and target_id. Server-owned settings_center providers build fixed edit descriptors; arbitrary source/object/url values from the model are forbidden.
Domain right-panel providers live in apps/settings_center/right_panel.py; apps.core remains a generic registry. The access fragment endpoint must be functional in the drawer by the end of package 06.
The generic ui.open_right_panel remains view-only. Applying changes always requires the human editor Save action.
AG-UI dependencies/profile and wire contract are unchanged.
acceptance: Direct Django permissions and their UI section are absent from product access explanations because no product enforcement policy reads them.
Role, superuser, technical-group, ACL, and workflow sources remain distinguishable.
Memory technical-group behavior is unchanged and no group merge occurs.
Inactive users have no effective capabilities; assigned membership facts are clearly non-effective.
AI can explain a selected user's effective access with a minimal privacy-safe payload and without PendingAction or any access-mutation tool.
AI user listing separates contract roles, technical groups and memory groups instead of returning one merged groups list.
AI can return a server-authorized command for the selected existing user or contract role; arbitrary targets and technical/memory groups fail closed.
The access tool contract validator permanently rejects access-domain write tools, and the runtime tools contract is migrated only through the reviewed path.
Applying changes still requires the human editor's Save action; package 06 owns final fragment rendering and browser acceptance.
